shots.focal_element: Colour-picker popover listing the Brand Kit palettes (Tropical Hotels, Tropical Motels, Tropical Group), left at full brightness while the rest of the editor is dimmed
shots.typography: Native product UI text: small sentence-case sans-serif labels in regular weight, normal tracking; the preview heading 'Welcome Screen' is a larger regular-weight sans. No added motion-graphics type.
shots.what_happens: A zoomed-in, held view of the theme editor: a dark overlay dims everything except the Brand Kit palette section of the colour popover, so the three saved palettes read as the subject. The frame is static across the shot, with the cursor resting on the colour dropdown. No narration falls inside the shot; it follows 'use our color palettes' (w179-w180).
shots.build_rebuild: Over a static, scaled-up screenshot of the editor, fade in a full-frame 50% dark overlay with a rounded-rect cut-out (mask) around the palette popover, hold for about 2 s, then fade the overlay out.

shots.focal_element: The mobile-preview Typeform welcome card, which turns from default white to the pink Tropical Hotels theme with a THG logo
shots.typography: All text is native product UI: small sentence-case sans-serif labels in regular weight with medium-weight section headers. After the theme is applied, the preview title and description switch to a serif face in a light colour, and the logo 'THG' is a bold serif wordmark. Font names cannot be read reliably, so none are given.
shots.what_happens: The spotlight dim from s015 lifts to show the full theme editor. 'Background image > Add' opens a Media Gallery modal with hotel and motel photos (w181-w182 'media gallery'), and the modal closes. 'Logo > Add' then opens a gallery with the THG logo variants (w183-w187 'and logo in the design'). Around 1:39 the preview card fills with the pink Tropical Hotels theme: serif type, a pale Start button and the THG logo top-left. The cursor then moves to 'Publish changes' (w188-w198 'Make sure to publish changes...'), and the shot crossfades into the Brand Kit themes page.
shots.build_rebuild: Play a cursor-guided screen recording at a fixed frame. Pop the media-gallery modal in and out with a soft shadow, then fade the preview card's colours, font and logo from the default theme to the branded theme over about 0.5 s, timed to the narration.

shots.focal_element: Row of three Brand Kit theme cards (pink Tropical Hotels, teal Tropical Motel, yellow Tropical Group)
shots.typography: Native product UI: small sentence-case sans-serif breadcrumb, tab and card labels in regular weight. The theme-card swatches preview 'Question' and 'Answer' in a serif face. Normal tracking throughout.
shots.what_happens: On the Themes tab of the Tropical Hotel Group Brand Kit, three finished theme cards sit in a row and the view holds on them while the narrator says 'Now that we have a collection of Brand Kit themes, let's apply them to a Typeform' (w199-w214). Near the end the cursor clicks the 'Brand kits' breadcrumb, which shows the Brand kits list (Headphone Corp, Tropical Hotel Group). That list then crossfades into the main workspace as 'Back in my workspace' (w215-w218) begins.
shots.build_rebuild: Hold a full-frame screenshot of the themes grid for about 5 s, cut to the brand-kits list screenshot on a simulated breadcrumb click, then crossfade over about 0.4 s to the workspace screen.

shots.focal_element: Typeform workspace grid of colourful form cards with the 'Create typeform' button
shots.typography: Native product UI: sentence-case sans-serif sidebar and toolbar labels in regular weight. The 'PRIVATE' and 'SHARED' section headers are small uppercase with wide tracking. Card titles are centred, medium-sized sans in white or dark text on coloured tiles.
shots.what_happens: This brief 0.9 s shot shows the main workspace. It lands on the tail of 'Back in my workspace' (w215-w218) to re-establish where the user is before a new Typeform is created. The cursor is at the top-left, and nothing else visibly changes within the shot.
shots.build_rebuild: Crossfade over about 0.4 s into a static full-frame workspace screenshot and hold it for under 1 s, as an establishing beat before the next action.
